queries.prompt: Explain the Cloud WAN Core Network Edge (CNE) route evaluation order and how inbound routing policies (`set-local-preference`) steer between multiple Direct Connect Gateways.
Why does Transit Gateway prefer our static Site-to-Site VPN route over our 10 Gbps Direct Connect BGP route for `10.10.0.0/16`?
Walk through how BGP local-preference communities `7224:7300`, `7224:7200`, and `7224:7100` vs AS-path prepending control AWS Direct Connect path selection.
We prepended our AS-path 6 times on our Mumbai Direct Connect VIF, yet `ap-south-1` traffic still refuses to shift to our Ireland Direct Connect VIF—why?
Packets leave on-prem over our IPsec VPN tunnel and come back from AWS over Direct Connect, causing our stateful firewall to drop the TCP return traffic. Why is AWS picking a different return path?
We attached two Direct Connect Gateways (`amazonSideAsn` 64512 and 64513) to our Transit Gateway expecting active-active ECMP, but only one attachment is installed as a next hop.

Our London Cloud WAN CNE is treating our 10G Equinix LD5 Slough Direct Connect circuit as a remote path instead of preferring it locally—check the evaluation rules and what `describe-connections` field explains this.

Given a VPC route table with `10.20.0.0/16 -> local`, `10.0.0.0/8 -> tgw-1`, `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-1`, and `pl-68a54001 -> vpce-s3`, trace which next hop wins for `10.20.5.0/24 -> eni-fw` and cross-region S3.
Three data centers (ASNs 65010, 65011, 65012) each advertise `10.1.0.0/16` into Cloud WAN via separate DXGWs—how do we make path selection deterministic under policy version `2025.11`?
Read this `tshark` packet capture CSV showing `tcp.analysis.retransmission` on 8960-byte frames while 64-byte pings succeed, and diagnose the issue.
Why does `auth.api.partner.io` return `NXDOMAIN` after we enabled `PrivateDnsEnabled=true` on a VPC Interface Endpoint for `api.partner.io`?
Compute the exact uncovered CIDR residual when `dxvif-bbb` advertises `10.10.0.0/22` and peer `dxvif-aaa` only advertises `10.10.1.0/24`.
